PullRequest.Title: Gate execution subagent turn-wise prompting
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add the advanced experimental `github.copilot.chat.executionSubagent.turnWisePrompting` setting
- preserve the legacy final-turn prompt when the setting is disabled
- show the remaining execution iterations on every turn when enabled
- add focused prompt rendering coverage for both behaviors

## Validation

- `cd extensions/copilot && npm run test:unit -- src/extension/prompts/node/agent/test/executionSubagentPrompt.spec.tsx`
- `cd extensions/copilot && npx eslint src/extension/prompt/node/executionSubagentToolCallingLoop.ts src/extension/prompts/node/agent/executionSubagentPrompt.tsx src/extension/prompts/node/agent/test/executionSubagentPrompt.spec.tsx src/platform/configuration/common/configurationService.ts`
- `npm run precommit`

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the execution subagent with turn-wise prompting disabled (the new default) and iterate through terminal-backed tool calls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each serialized loop iteration builds the prompt, then performs one model network request; if the model requests the terminal tool, that subprocess completes before the next model iteration. The added configuration read occurs during prompt construction but is a synchronous lookup against cached VS Code configuration and in-memory experiment treatments, not an I/O boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the rendered execution-subagent messages to endpoint.makeChatRequest2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model request per loop iteration, bounded by the existing execution-subagent tool-call limit (default 10); iterations are serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model request occurred once per iteration; every prompt also carried the remaining-iterations user message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each request is on the subagent critical path, but the diff does not add requests or concurrency. With the default disabled setting, non-final prompts contain one fewer short user message than before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/agent/executionSubagentPrompt.tsx:46 system instruction and ChatToolCalls at line 79
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The model may invoke CoreRunInTerminal, whose result is rendered into the next prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one terminal invocation per model turn by the execution prompt contract, with total turns bounded by the existing tool-call limit; actual calls depend on model output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same terminal tool and serialization rules applied; the model additionally saw a countdown message on each turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous terminal calls block the next iteration; timed-out/background calls stop exposing tools. The diff does not add or move terminal execution onto this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render the optional iteration guidance into chat messages for request serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per prompt render, normally once per iteration, with an existing possible second render when a background command is first detected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A short remaining-iterations message was rendered on every turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Default behavior removes the guidance from non-final turns and substitutes a similarly small final-turn message, so it does not increase serialized prompt size or render work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of execution-subagent iterations, bounded by the configured tool-call limit (default 10), plus the existing one-time rerender when a background command is first discovered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Iterations within one execution-subagent invocation are sequential. Model and terminal work are not fanned out by this diff; aggregate concurrency across independent parent invocations is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The endpoint promise is cached per loop. Configuration is read from cached VS Code configuration and in-memory treatment values on each render. The diff adds no result cache and defeats no existing tool-result or endpoint cache; default prompts are slightly smaller, while enabled prompts match the pre-diff shape.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no code-level work amplification or boundary increase is introduced on this path; any behavioral effect on model-selected iteration count is speculative.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model behavior may differ when the countdown is hidden, but there is no deterministic evidence that this increases turns or terminal calls; the loop's existing hard bound is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The default path reduces prompt content before the final turn, and the opt-in path preserves the pre-diff per-turn prompt.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the execution subagent with turn-wise prompting enabled by user setting or experiment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each iteration performs the same local configuration lookup and prompt render before the existing serialized model request. The new branch selects the same remaining-iterations message that the base revision rendered unconditionally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one model request for each subagent iteration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per iteration, bounded by the existing configured limit; no batching or parallelism changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-turn network request cadence and iteration-guidance payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network latency remains on the critical path exactly as before; the opt-in prompt payload preserves the prior message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute a model-selected terminal command and include its result in a subsequent turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one terminal command per turn under the prompt contract, bounded by the same turn limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical terminal-tool exposure and execution flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No scheduling, cancellation, or fan-out behavior changes when the flag is enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the remaining-iterations user message into each prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One short message per render, as in the base revision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same message was always serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No payload growth relative to the pre-diff behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Execution turns up to the existing configured limit and any unchanged concurrent parent-agent invocations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One in-flight iteration per loop; no new limiter, queue, burst, or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Endpoint and tool-result caching are unchanged. The enabled prompt shape matches the base revision, so no new cache-key growth or cache invalidation mechanism is established.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that enabled mode adds no performance cost relative to the base revision beyond a cheap local boolean lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Experiment prevalence is unknown, but mechanism comparison is exact: enabled behavior is equivalent to the base prompt.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression because this mode preserves the pre-diff work and boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load Copilot extension configuration metadata and expose the new advanced experimental setting.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: VS Code parses the existing extension manifest during extension discovery/registration; the added localization string and boolean schema entry are static metadata and do not trigger runtime filesystem or network operations from the changed code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed addition of one boolean configuration property and one localized description, independent of workspace size or session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work or concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration metadata follows the existing manifest/configuration cache lifecycle; the diff introduces no growing key set or retained per-workspace objects.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the static metadata addition cannot produce an actionable startup regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Manifest parsing cost is not measured, but the fixed-size schema addition has no realistic scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the added startup work is constant and negligible.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all six changed files. Traced prompt construction through the serialized tool-calling loop, model network request, terminal subprocess path, configuration lookup, endpoint/tool-result caches, and manifest registration. The default branch removes prompt content on earlier turns, while the enabled branch reproduces the base behavior; no changed line adds boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, concurrency bursts, or meaningful repeated work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
